flags.summary: The rep solicited the prospect's cash on hand and his savings and checking account balances on a recorded first sales call; the prospect declined and apologised for being caught off guard.
evidence: First thing, what's your cash on hand right now that you could put down today for this?
What's your savings account or checking account?
I'm just reluctant to say anything because I really didn't even know.
It's, I'm just a little, I don't know, I'm just a little caught off guard. Sorry, man.

flags.summary: The rep moved the follow-up relationship onto his personal WhatsApp number, continuing a pattern of sales contact leaving recorded and company-controlled channels.
evidence: Now, if anything comes up, do you use WhatsApp? Yeah. Okay. Yeah. I can give you my personal number. I will shoot you a text.
So whenever something comes up during the weekend or on Monday when you're going to have a discussion with your wife or whatever, just hit me up.

flags.summary: The rep endorsed a six-month timeline for a Boston Marathon qualifier — a 41-minute improvement on the prospect's own race predictor — without establishing that the programme or the coach does distance-running coaching at all.
evidence: Okay, so actually we have six months to work on that, so you can actually go for the qualifier.
So for you specifically, Trevor will adapt that program to your running schedule, because that also needs to be adjusted.
Let's just say 3 hours 10 minutes. That's, what, 41 minutes faster than what I'm predicted to right now?
So Bill, from what I'm hearing, definitely Trevor can help you with your goals
